topicName: APIViews, GenericViews, and ViewSets with Routers

[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Django REST Framework: APIViews, GenericViews, and ViewSets with Routers"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django REST Framework (DRF) provides multiple abstractions for building APIs, ranging from low-level function-based views to highly automated ViewSets. Choosing the right tool depends on your requirement for control versus rapid development."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. APIView: Maximum Control"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The APIView class subclasses Django's standard View class. It handles request parsing, authentication, and permission checking explicitly. Use APIViews when you need complete custom logic that does not fit standard CRUD patterns."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework import status
from .models import Item
from .serializers import ItemSerializer

class ItemListAPIView(APIView):
    def get(self, request):
        items = Item.objects.all()
        serializer = ItemSerializer(items, many=True)
        return Response(serializer.data)

    def post(self, request):
        serializer = ItemSerializer(data=request.data)
        if serializer.is_valid():
            serializer.save()
            return Response(serializer.data, status=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
        return Response(serializer.errors, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. GenericViews: Reusable Mixins"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generic API views combine common database patterns with DRF views. By combining mixins like ListModelMixin and CreateModelMixin with GenericAPIView, you drastically reduce boilerplate code."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from rest_framework import generics
from .models import Item
from .serializers import ItemSerializer

class ItemListCreateGenericView(generics.ListCreateAPIView):
    queryset = Item.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ItemSerializer

class ItemRetrieveUpdateDestroyGenericView(generics.RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView):
    queryset = Item.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ItemSerializer"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. ViewSets and Routers: Ultimate Efficiency"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"ViewSets combine the logic for a set of related views into a single class. Instead of writing separate views for listing, creating, retrieving, updating, and destroying, you manage them in one place. Coupled with Routers, URLs are generated automatically."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from rest_framework import viewsets
from .models import Item
from .serializers import ItemSerializer

class ItemViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Item.objects.all()
    serializer_class = ItemSerializer"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To wire up the ViewSet using a DefaultRouter, configure your urls.py like this:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from django.urls import path, include
from rest_framework.routers import DefaultRouter
from .views import ItemViewSet

router = DefaultRouter()
router.register(r'items', ItemViewSet, basename='item')

urlpatterns = [
    path('', include(router.urls)),
]"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use APIView when implementing custom business logic or external integrations that deviate from standard database operations."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use GenericViews when you need standard CRUD operations but require explicit control over individual endpoint mapping."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ViewSets and Routers for standard REST APIs to maximize code reuse and automate URL configuration."}]
